question: What will be the ending value of the UST 10Y Yield for these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 21 - Oct 2)

calls.reasoning: Reference class first: over 10-business-day windows the 10Y yield is near a random walk, so the anchor is the Sep 18 level (~5.00-5.01%) plus this year's median 10bd drift (~+1 to +3bp), i.e. ~5.01. Adjustments are small and two-sided: bearish are the Sep 16 hike with another signaled (53% for October), core PCE ~3.3% y/y, $104 oil on the Iran war, soft 10Y TIPS demand (2.24x bid-to-cover, weakest since Sep 2025), BoJ tightening and heavy corporate/AI supply; bullish are visible real-money demand at the 5% handle, the Treasury buyback program, profit-taking that already produced a 6bp rally Sep 17, and quarter-end index extension buying Sep 30. Net drift ~+1bp, so the median sits at spot. The binding decision is tail width: with SD ~0.18 over 10 sessions and a payrolls report on resolution morning, the open upper bound at 5.255 is only ~1.4 SD away and a +25bp fortnight occurred twice in the last month, so I price 9% escape above; -150bp to the lower bound has no precedent and is left unpriced. No tradable market matched this contract (Kalshi weekly series returned no open markets; nothing on Polymarket/Manifold), so nothing to blend.

Down: buyback program and reported reluctance to be short the long end, the 9/17 rally showing two-way flow at the 5% handle, a 19-year-high level attracting yield buyers, quarter-end extension demand, equity-market stress from high yields.

- Implied vol: MOVE index 77.88 on Sep 1, 75.32 early September, 73.10 on Sep 4 (MacroMicro); it reached ~115 in March 2026 right after the Iran conflict began. A MOVE of 80 implies ~5.0bp/day; 90 implies ~5.7bp/day.

calls.reconciliation: Settled factually: spot is ~5.00 (three independent Sep 18 quotes vs one stale Sep 17 par print of 4.94); payrolls confirmed for Oct 2 08:30 ET, before the 20:00Z resolution; no tradable contract exists on any venue the three runs could reach (Kalshi KXTNOTED/KXTNOTEW series exist but returned no price, one run hit HTTP 429; nothing on Polymarket/Manifold/bookmakers), so nothing was blended. Dispersion was the real spread: I reconciled the three estimates (0.38/0.41/0.42) to 0.41 on a blended realized/implied SD of ~0.16, rejecting both the low end (ignores the post-payrolls resolution print) and the pure unconditional 18-22bp (higher than current realized vol). I discarded Run 3's stated reason for shading its escape to 8% — it cites a 'Polymarket touch ladder' its own dossier says did not exist — but kept 8% as the level, since a normal with SD 0.16 gives ~6% past +25.5bp and fat tails plus a live hot-PCE/Hormuz mechanism justify a modest uplift. Remaining dispute is pure judgment — whether to extrapolate the September uptrend. I take the martingale reading: two-week yield momentum is weak and the last two sessions traded both ways, so I would bet on spot, not on continuation. I carry the runs' shared reference class (unconditional 10bd DGS10 changes, median ~0) forward because I agree with it.

disagreements.claim: The +9.6bp/window September drift should be extrapolated into the window
disagreements.verdict: No — 10-day yield momentum is weak and Sep 17/18 traded both directions at the 5% handle; median held at spot, shaded to 4.99 by upper truncation

disagreements.claim: Upper escape above 5.255 is 7% vs 8% vs 9%
disagreements.verdict: 8% — Gaussian baseline ~6% at 1.5 SD, uplifted for fat tails, the post-payrolls print, and two +20bp+ fortnights this month

calls.reference_class: 10-business-day changes in the UST 10Y yield (FRED DGS10), 2024-2026 unconditional — median change ~0, i.e. the level is a near-martingale at this horizon
